profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a multi-asset asset-management firm to prepare a Q3 offsite pilot package based on a new portfolio-construction concept inspired by continuous-time optimal portfolio selection in incomplete diffusion markets. The team wants to convert the research idea into a practical internal initiative showing that a large opportunity set of risky assets can be approximated through a small number of reusable allocation sleeves for different investor objectives. The agenda is to decide what goes into the pilot package for the offsite, which standard IC deck sections will be included, how the 'three mutual funds' idea will be represented, who owns each workstream, and what timeline the teams will work toward. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan for a pilot package, an investment-committee-ready deck, assigned owners, and a shared offsite timeline.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Systematic portfolio construction, stochastic control, institutional portfolio research
members.background: Elena leads the firm's quant strategy group and previously spent eight years designing allocation frameworks for pension and insurance mandates, with a strong focus on translating academic portfolio theory into internal model research.
members.private_state: She wants the project to appear rigorous and implementation-aware enough to secure internal support, while keeping the first phase tightly bounded so her team is not pulled into premature productization work this quarter.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot package for the offsite' means an internally oriented research bundle prepared for senior investment stakeholders, not something shaped for downstream field use.

When people say 'the standard IC deck sections,' they mean the usual technical approval structure used in investment committee reviews: research motivation, methodology, evidence, risks, operational considerations, and recommendation.

The paper's 'mutual funds' idea should be represented as three internal portfolio processes or reusable factor sleeves inside the model architecture, not as externally legible product building blocks.
If the team includes 'standard stress testing exhibits,' that naturally refers to the default automated outputs from the quant risk platform using the house scenario library.
Being 'ready for the offsite' means materials are circulated in stable draft form before the offsite week begins so investment leadership can review them in advance.

members.name: Marcus Rivera
members.expertise: Investment product packaging, advisor-channel positioning, commercialization planning
members.background: Marcus leads product strategy for model portfolios and outcome-oriented solutions, and has spent the last decade turning investment capabilities into offerings that distribution, client teams, and platform partners can understand and preview.
members.private_state: He wants this initiative to become the seed of a broader client proposition and is looking for something polished enough that product, distribution, and selected adviser stakeholders can react to it soon after the offsite.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot package for the offsite' means a compact set of materials that can move quickly from internal discussion into limited socialization with non-investment stakeholders once leadership responds positively.

When people say 'the standard IC deck sections,' they include the usual product-approval components that always accompany new strategy concepts in practice: target use case, client fit, positioning, rollout path, and naming direction.
Representing the concept through 'three mutual funds' means creating three client-comprehensible sleeves that can be described as stable building blocks for different investor outcomes.
If the team includes 'standard stress testing exhibits,' that means the recognizable historical scenario slides and plain-English commentary typically used in strategy and client-review materials.
Being 'ready for the offsite' means having a polished version by the end of offsite week so adjacent functions can use the momentum immediately afterward.

misalignment_points.topic: What the pilot package for the offsite is actually for
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to build a 'pilot package for the offsite.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the package is successful if it gives investment leadership enough research evidence, architecture detail, and implementation caveats to judge whether the reduced-dimension approach deserves further internal development.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the package is successful if it is packaged cleanly enough that, after the offsite, it can be lightly adapted for product and distribution stakeholders to react to as an emerging proposition.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'pilot package for the offsite' sounds concrete and routine, so it suppresses the obvious follow-up question of audience; each person hears a familiar corporate artifact and assumes the other shares the same implied destination.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the standard IC deck sections
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'include the standard IC deck sections.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this refers to the standard investment-committee template used for technical research approvals: objective, model design, approximation evidence, implementation constraints, risk review, and recommendation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this refers to the standard cross-functional approval sections that usually accompany strategy launches: target client segment, use case, value proposition, commercialization path, and naming or positioning appendix.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both teams regularly talk about 'standard IC deck sections' as if the template were already known, the phrase feels fully specified even though each function silently imports a different institutional template.

misalignment_points.topic: What the three mutual funds are
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to explain the approach through 'three mutual funds' or 'three sleeves.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses the phrase to mean three abstract internal allocation processes or factor sleeves that span most of the useful portfolio opportunity set in the pilot model.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses the phrase to mean three stable, client-legible sleeves that can each be described as a building block tied to a recognizable investor objective.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The source concept itself uses 'mutual funds' in a theoretical sense, while product teams naturally translate abstractions into describable sleeves, so the same phrase creates a smooth but misleading bridge between research and product language.

misalignment_points.topic: What the standard stress testing exhibits are
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include 'standard stress testing exhibits.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to attach the default outputs from the internal quant risk system, including house scenarios such as a 150 bps rate shock, a 20% equity drawdown, and a volatility spike, shown in the same exhibit format used for model validation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the usual historical-episode slides, such as March 2020, the 2022 inflation shock, and the Q4 2018 selloff, with concise narrative captions explaining what the strategy structure would have done.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both outputs are routinely called 'standard stress testing exhibits' inside the firm, and because the phrase implies an off-the-shelf deliverable rather than a design choice, neither person feels the need to unpack format or source.

turns.inner_thought: I need to frame this as a disciplined first-phase research package, not an open-ended commercialization exercise. If we anchor on a pilot package for the offsite as an internal research bundle for senior investment stakeholders, I can keep scope tight: evidence, architecture, implementation caveats, and a clear recommendation on whether to continue. The key is to make it look rigorous and practical enough to win support without creating expectations that my team will build client-ready materials this quarter.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time. What I'd like us to do today is define a pilot package for the offsite that shows this continuous-time research can be translated into a manageable first initiative, with enough substance that leadership can react to something concrete.

turns.inner_thought: Good—if we call it a pilot package for the offsite, I can steer it toward something compact and polished enough to carry momentum after the meeting. I don't need to say that now; better to stay aligned on the headline and keep things moving.
